paragraphs: The GLS63 AMG has been the range-topping performance variant of Mercedes' full-size SUV since its introduction on the X166 generation in 2012, continuing through to the current X167 generation. The first-generation GLS63 (then badged as GL63 AMG) used the M157 - a 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8, a well-known AMG powerplant from that era. The current X167-generation car switched to the M177 - a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 shared with a wide range of AMG models, including the GLE63 and S63. Both engines are hand-built AMG units, and both share a similar pattern of valve seal and coolant system wear over time - which is why we address these components as standard on every GLS63 AMG rebuild, regardless of which generation you own.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLS63 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 fitted to the GLS63 AMG (and previously the GL63 AMG) from 2012 to 2019. Known for valve seal and coolant system wear - see the callout above. We replace valve seals, timing chain components, coolant components and bearings as standard on every M157 rebuild.

A 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 fitted to the current-generation GLS63 AMG from 2019 onwards. Shares a similar valve seal and coolant system wear pattern with its predecessor. We replace valve seals, timing chain components, coolant components and bearings as standard on every M177 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLS63 AMG spans two distinct twin-turbo V8 engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming an M157 part will work on an M177 car - risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic GLS quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
